item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Sun Sep 27 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Tue Sep 29, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

Follow your guide deep into the night in one of our two-person Scoot Coupes as they lead you on a hair-raising adventure, traveling along eerie back roads, zipping past the pumpkin patch, making stops to hear local folklore and the lesser-known haunted side of Lancaster County. A guided tour of Lancaster County’s back roads, after sundown Featuring local folklore and stories of the eerie side of Lancaster Who knows, there might be a surprise or two along the way.

item.title: The Haunting of Pumpkin Junction at Strasburg Rail Road — Fri Oct 2 — Strasburg Rail Road
item.description:
Grab your family and head on down to the 1978 annual Pumpkin Junction Fall Festival, where we celebrate the last Fall train with games, food and, most importantly, the yearly Pumpkin carving contest. But when the contest is mysteriously sabotaged, our gang of amateur sleuths make it their mission to uncover the mystery that lies behind this year’s old tradition. Be a part of the mystery as our group tries to solve the case of the Haunting of Pumpkin Junction. Our show begins 15 minutes before boarding, at our Town Square Stage right at the heart of the station, so please plan to arrive 30 minutes before departure so you don’t miss even one second of this mysterious adventure! The show will continue aboard our beautiful historic train cars and conclude back at the station, so stick around after deboarding and head back over to the Town Square Stage for the haunting conclusion of our mystery.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Gothic Echoes — Fri Oct 2, 8:00 PM — First Reformed Church
item.description:
Organist Larry Hershey will perform the program “Gothic Echoes” at First Reformed Church of Lancaster. The free 30 minute concert will include:Bach’s world-famous “Toccata in D Minor”Charles Gounod’s “Funeral March for a Marionette” (which became familiar as the musical theme for Alfred Hitchcock’s TV mystery series) “Come, Holy Spirit” by Maurice Durufle.Leon Boellmann’s “Toccata” from Suite Gothique.
Mr. Hershey will be playing The Hill Byrne/Christiansen Memorial Organ in First Reformed’s historic 1854 sanctuary at 40 E. Orange Street in downtown Lancaster. The First Friday “Organic Reflections” concert series is a gift to the community from First Reformed Church, a center city congregation of the United Church of Christ. Doors open at 7:30 pm.
Learn More
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Character Design-Materials and Techniques: Grades 4-6 at PCA&D — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM — Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration
item.description:
In this hands-on character design class, middle school artists will learn the fundamentals of creating original characters while discovering how different art materials shape their designs. Throughout the class, students will create at least two character designs using different material combinations, exploring how each medium affects the visual style, texture, and mood of their characters. Does watercolor create a softer, more whimsical feel? Do markers produce bold, graphic designs? Students will discover the answers through creative experimentation! Expect your child to have a mixture of lecture and plenty of space to creatively experiment.
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Playing with Symmetry – Flower Pounded Banners: Grades 7-9 at PCA&D — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM — Pennsylvania College of Art & Design – Center for Creative Exploration
item.description:
In this session students will work with early fall flowers and foliage to create a flower pounded wall hanging! Artist and educator Christina Lukac will lead this hands on workshop where students will be able to experiment with the art of tataki-zomé or “plant bashing”. Students will be able to make flower prints by gently hammering flowers and foliage into natural fiber fabric. Students will learn the centuries old method of using natural objects in artwork, receive a guided demonstration from the instructor, and have lots of studio time to create. Students will leave this session with the knowledge of a new technique and a flower pounded banner to take home!
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.title: Sparkdate: Tellus AfterDark — Tue Oct 6, 6:30 PM — Tellus360
item.description:
A downtown Lancaster staple with a rooftop that turns any night into something worth dressing up for. Open sky, string lights, and a bar that’s easy to linger at — the kind of place that does half the work of making people comfortable before anyone even says hello. Add real conversations instead of small talk that goes nowhere, and you’ve got a night built for singles who actually want to meet someone, not just match with them.
How the night works:Check in with a host and get a name tag — there’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements:First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play — that’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold — and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. item.title: Redemption Time — Tue Oct 6, 7:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
Join us at the Ware Center for a free screening of the film Redemption Time—plus a community discussion panel and a Q&A with the filmmakers. Witness a powerful multimedia performance film featuring poet Jimmy Santiago Baca and jazz violinist Christian Howes, two formerly incarcerated artists who reclaimed their lives through art. Combining spoken word, music, and visual art, Redemption Time invites audiences into a shared space of healing and transformation.
Come early for a pre-show community panel at 6:15 pm, and stay after the film for a post-screening Q&A with Dr. David Gonzalez, director of Redemption Time, and Christian Howes, a formerly incarcerated individual featured in Redemption Time and an award-winning jazz violinist. Admission is free! Tickets are required for entry.
Register Now
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.description:
Creepadama puts a spooky spin on the Japanese art of Kokedama — a “moss ball” planting style where living moss wraps around a ball of soil to create a unique botanical sculpture. Create your own haunted moss garden complete with creepy embellishments, webs, and eerie details. You’ll learn the history behind Kokedama, how to care for your creation, and leave with a one-of-a-kind plant that’s a little bit spooky and a whole lot alive.

Get ready to squish, scoop, and explore at our Pumpkin Guts Sensory Play event!Designed specifically for curious toddlers, this hands-on, delightfully messy morning invites little learners to dive headfirst into the textures, colors, and smells of autumn. Instead of just looking at pumpkins, your child will get to experience them from the inside out! Toddlers can sink their hands into cold, gooey pumpkin pulp, and separate the slippery seeds It is the ultimate tactile experience to stimulate brain development, language skills, and spatial awareness in a supportive, social environment. Recommended for ages 1-3. Registration is required to make sure every child has a pumpkin!What to Wear: Dress for a mess! Please join us and the Elizabethtown Area Democrats as we go door to door talking to neighbors about our Democratic candidates: Senator James Malone (SD-36) and Hugh Darlington (HD-98) NO EXPERIENCE NECESSARY.
